pr_title: Add specialized FrozenSet implementations for byte and char
pr_comments: Can you point to some places where `FrozenSet<byte>` and `FrozenSet<char>` will be used?

Should be similar to `SearchValues<byte>`/`SearchValues<char>`, where you'd previously be using e.g. `HashSet` / `string.Contains` / `bool[128]`.
Many uses would benefit from using `SearchValues`'s `ContainsAny` though as they're just doing scalar loops around `Contains` themselves.

As a random example, here's one in Uri, though we could of course use `SearchValues` since we know the implementation:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a29d5f97d0913c83bb8092ab9eebfd7ef5bdd3d9/src/libraries/System.Private.Uri/src/System/UriHelper.cs#L548

My main motivation was making the answer to "what should I use for `Contains(T)` checks" simply `FrozenSet<T>`, given that the interesting part of the implementation can be rather easily shared with `SearchValues` in this case.

You decided it wasn't worthwhile?

Another option, if you think there is value in it, would be to only have the optimization on core and literally just wrap SearchValues.

I was intrigued by #111886 and wanted to play around with how that would look like for bitmap based `FrozenSet`, and a perfect hash based `FrozenSet`/`FrozenDictionary`.
Something like
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/compare/main...MihaZupan:frozenset-bytechar3

That would merge `ByteFrozenSet` and `Latin1CharFrozenSet` from this PR into a single impl, even if it'd be a few cycles slower.

Not sure it's worth having the specialization for all the types though, even if generics makes it relatively "cheap" code-wise.

issue_context.title: Consider improving FrozenSet for byte/char
issue_context.body:
`FrozenSet<T>` is the go-to option if you have an arbitary set of values and just need to do a bunch of `Contains(T)` queries.
Now that `SearchValues<T>` is a thing, I've seen the question posed a few times of whether one should use that instead, as it also has a `Contains(T)`.

Currently for the best performance you'd want to use `FrozenSet` for everything _except `byte`/`char`_, where `SearchValues` will do a better job.
`SearchValues<string>.Contains` on the other hand is strictly worse as we're just backing it with a `HashSet<string>`.

We should consider improving `FrozenSet` to be as good as `SearchValues` for these two types to make the decision/recommendations easy.

(part of the issue is also that existing docs on `SearchValues` don't make it obvious that the point of the type is to use it with extension methods on spans)

---

In practice the interesting cases here IMO are:
- using a bitmap when all the values are ASCII
- consider borrowing the [perfect-hash](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ce9dd2ad46a4842f5cf0f03c4a30b4d29bd0b4cc/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/SearchValues/ProbabilisticMapState.cs#L24-L30) O(1) lookup that doesn't need to walk over entries to confirm matches.

review_comments: The name of this class is a little confusing since this is now just a generic char collection/lookup. For example, IndexOfAnyExcept for non-ASCII will not use the ProbMap at all but it is using the hash table.

I don't see why the meaning would change with this PR, the type is still the state needed for probabilistic `SearchValues` implementations. The probabilstic part won't be used for `-Except` because it can't be, but we still need some state to implement the fallback even if most of that implementation was extracted to a separate type.

Did you have a better name in mind?

A CharSet/CharLookup utility might be useful to refactor out and have the ProbabilisticMap hold it (instead of this class holding a ProbabilisticMap). Not sure how useful it would really be though and I don't think it's in the scope of this PR.
Doing the vectorized popcount ran faster on my machine (~25%). Vector256 doesn't have popcount so I used the software fallback but just with 8x32.

This `int Count()` helper is not on the hot path, it'll only be called once during `FrozenSet` creation. I don't think it's worth complicating the code for that in this case. E.g. you could also special-case Arm64 and do 2x `Vector128` `PopCount`s there.

For char and byte you might want to consider overriding `IsProperSubsetOfCore`, etc. which take IEnumerable<T> since the concrete class could be string, char[] or byte[] a lot of the time. If so, this can be optimized to use vectorization later on like search values.

I did see that, but wasn't sure how important those methods were (I've never used anything other than `Contains` myself). I'd prefer to leave that as-is for now, seems like a perfectly good thing for a follow up PR though.
